title: Ramified completed coefficient quotient comparison
statement: Let l be prime, E and L finite extensions of Q_l, and ι:E→L a Q_l-algebra embedding. Suppose e≥1, the ideal generated by ι(varpi_E) equals (varpi_L^e), index(e,n)+1=e(n+1), and j_n:O_E/(varpi_E^(n+1))→O_L/(varpi_L^(index(e,n)+1)) sends each residue of a to the residue of ι(a). For each scheme W there is a Coefficients datum of def-weil-ramified-pullback-tower-data: the completed inclusion, its same-index and ramified projection equations, the normalized scalar extension isomorphisms for coefficient modules, and their finite quotient transition equation. This is the coefficient part alone and asserts no pullback comparison or ramification existence.

proof.text:
Use the compatible same-index maps $\iota_n$ and projections of the scalar-extension definition to define $c_W:R_W\to S_W$ by $\pi^L_n c_W=(\iota_n)_W\pi^E_n$. Its component at $n=em$ factors through $B_{E,W,m}$: the map $\mathcal O_E/t^{em}\to\mathcal O_L/v^{em}$ kills $t^m$ by Step 1, and its factor is exactly $j_m$. Consequently $\pi^L_{em}c_W=(j_m)_W\pi^E_m$. This proves the coefficient square needed at every level, rather than assuming that the same-index map is already an isomorphism. Put $R^E_W=R_W$ and $R^L_W=S_W$. Write $r^F:g^{-1}R^F_Y\to R^F_X$ for the completed structure maps induced by the finite projections and $c^g_{A_{F,n}}$. At every level $n$, naturality of the constant-ring maps gives
$$(\iota_n)_X c^g_{A_{E,n}}=c^g_{A_{L,n}}g^{-1}(\iota_n)_Y.$$
Indeed their adjoints extend the same map of constant presheaves, sending $a$ to its included residue on $X$, so sheafification gives equality. After projection to $B_{L,X,n}$, both $c_Xr^E$ and $r^Lg^{-1}c_Y$ are therefore
$$(\iota_n)_X c^g_{A_{E,n}}g^{-1}\pi^E_{Y,n}.$$
The limit universal property yields $c_Xr^E=r^Lg^{-1}c_Y$. This proves compatibility on the completed coefficient sheaves by their finite projections.

proof.text: Apply the canonical quotient clause of the constant-completion equivalence to $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(t)$ on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and to $A=\mathcal O_L$, $I=(v)$ on the same site. Noetherianity was checked in Step 1; the sites are taken small in the sheaf universe. Thus the actual limit projections induce $R_W/t^mR_W\cong B_{E,W,m}$ and $S_W/v^{em}S_W\cong B_{L,W,em}$. The constants $u,u^{-1}$ define mutually inverse sections of $S_W$, so Step 1 gives equality of ideal sheaves $t^mS_W=v^{em}S_W$. Hence $B_{L,W,em}$ is canonically $S_W/t^mS_W$ with its actual projection from $S_W$. This uses the degree-zero quotient clause only, and imposes no completeness or flatness condition on $P$.

proof.text: For $R=R_W$, $S=S_W$, the map $(R/t^mR)\otimes_R S\to S/t^mS$ sends $\bar r\otimes s$ to $\overline{c_W(r)s}$. Its inverse sends $\bar s$ to $\bar1\otimes s$: changing $s$ by $t^m s'$ changes the image by $\bar1\otimes t^m s'=\overline{t^m}\otimes s'=0$. The two composites are identities, since $\bar1\otimes c_W(r)s=\bar r\otimes s$. These bilinear formulas commute with restriction, and therefore define inverse maps of the sheaf tensor products, including when quotient sections lift only after a cover. Combine with Step 3. By the coefficient square in Step 2 the resulting coefficient isomorphism is precisely $\bar a\otimes s\mapsto j_m(\bar a)\pi^L_{em}(s)$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor; explicit quotient inverse using Tag 093M as established in Step 3

proof.text:
Write $q^F_{b,a}$ for quotient reduction from level $b$ to $a$. On quotient representatives,
$$q^L_{e(m+1),em}j_{m+1}(\bar a)=j_m q^E_{m+1,m}(\bar a),\qquad q^L_{e(m+1),em}\pi^L_{e(m+1)}(s)=\pi^L_{em}(s).$$
Both first expressions are the residue of the same element of $\mathcal O_E$ in $\mathcal O_L/v^{em}$; the second equality is the limit-projection identity. Applying these equations to $\bar a,b,s$ in Step 6 shows that its two transition composites both have image $(g^{-1}((p\otimes1)\otimes j_m(q^E_{m+1,m}\bar a)))\otimes(j_m(q^E_{m+1,m}b)\pi^L_{em}(s))$. Thus $\widetilde d_\bullet$ is a map of the specified towers, including their restricted completed-scalar actions. For a chain map $f:P\to P'$, either composite replaces $p$ by $f(p)$ in Step 6 and leaves the coefficient factors unchanged. The pure pairings determine tensor maps, so these generator equalities are equalities of sheaf maps, also on sections that require covers.

theorem coefficients_exists (e : ℕ) (he : 1 ≤ e)
    (hideal : Ideal.span ({integralScalarIntegerInclusion l E L ι
      (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E)} :
        Set (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l L)) =
      Ideal.span {Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l L ^ e})
    (hexp : ∀ n : ℕ, index e n + 1 = e * (n + 1))
    (j : ∀ n : ℕ, Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1) →+*
      Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l L (index e n + 1))
    (hj : ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E),
      j n (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Padic.coefficientExtensionIdeal l E (n + 1)) a) =
        Ideal.Quotient.mk (Padic.coefficientExtensionIdeal l L (index e n + 1))
          (integralScalarIntegerInclusion l E L ι a)) (W : Scheme.{t}) :
    Nonempty (Coefficients l E L ι e j W)
